summary:
# PAWPRINT MARS

PAWPRINT MARS is an interactive platform designed to help astronauts explore Mars safely and efficiently.

Our project focuses on Jezero Crater, using real data from NASA and USGS, including maps, images, and geological information, to help astronauts understand their surroundings and plan their missions.

The platform offers **route planning**, allowing astronauts to choose the shortest, fastest, or safest path while identifying potentially dangerous terrain.

It also includes an **Expedition Log**, where astronauts can save photos, record observations, and document discoveries.

Another key feature is our **Water Evidence Heatmap**, which highlights areas that may contain evidence of ancient water activity. The algorithm combines mineral indicators (45%), geological formations (40%), and terrain characteristics (15%) to calculate an evidence score for each location.

The heatmap does not predict where water exists today. Instead, it helps astronauts identify promising locations for investigating Mars's watery past.

By combining scientific data, navigation tools, and exploration records in one place, **PAWPRINT MARS makes Martian exploration safer, simpler, and more organized.**
details:
PAWPRINT MARS | Project Description

PAWPRINT MARS is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform that transforms real NASA and USGS scientific data into an accessible tool for navigating and investigating the Martian surface. Our goal is to help future explorers plan safer, more scientifically meaningful missions while making Mars exploration understandable to everyone.

How does it work?

The platform combines satellite imagery, digital terrain models, geological maps, mineral observations, and NASA Perseverance mission data into a layered interactive map of Jezero Crater. Users can select destinations, explore scientific locations, and compare three routes: Fastest, Shortest, and Lower Risk. Our A* pathfinding algorithm analyzes terrain elevation, slope, and estimated travel difficulty to calculate routes and highlight potential hazards.

One of our key innovations is the Water Evidence Explorer, a predictive scientific-priority heatmap. It combines mineral indicators from NASA's CRISM instrument (45%), geological formations (40%), and terrain characteristics (15%) to identify locations worth investigating for evidence of ancient water activity. The scores reflect our own transparent exploration model, not confirmed water deposits or probabilities of finding water.

The platform also includes NASA rover imagery, scientific information about Martian rock samples, simulated mission-resource planning, and an Expedition Log where explorers can document observations and mission progress.

Benefits and intended impact

PAWPRINT MARS brings scientific discovery and navigation together in one platform. Instead of requiring users to interpret complex datasets separately, it translates them into understandable visual layers, route comparisons, warnings, and scientific explanations.

Our intended impact is to support future mission-planning research, improve accessibility to planetary science, and inspire students and the public to participate in Mars exploration. With future access to higher-resolution terrain measurements and robotic sensors, the platform could support more precise hazard detection and navigation.

Tools and technologies

We developed the platform using React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, Python, and Leaflet for interactive mapping, scientific data processing, visualization, and route planning. Our routing system uses the A algorithm*, while terrain calculations use elevation measurements derived from NASA and USGS datasets.

Our scientific sources include HiRISE and CTX terrain data, CRISM mineral observations, USGS geological maps, and NASA Perseverance mission records. We also used AI development tools, including Claude Code and ChatGPT, to support coding, research, interface design, and development. No custom hardware was required; the project uses publicly available observations collected by existing Mars missions.

Creativity and design considerations

What makes PAWPRINT MARS creative is its combination of scientific exploration, route optimization, and evidence-based destination discovery. Rather than simply displaying a map, it helps users understand where to explore, why a location matters scientifically, and what terrain challenges may lie along the way.

We designed the interface to be visually engaging and approachable, with a friendly astronaut-dog mascot, clear explanations, interactive scientific layers, and an intuitive mission-planning experience.

Throughout development, we considered terrain resolution, astronaut safety, computational efficiency, data reliability, scientific uncertainty, accessibility, and ease of use. We also carefully distinguish simulated mission features from real NASA observations and ensure that our predictive scores are presented as scientific exploration priorities rather than proven discoveries.

Our vision is to make Mars exploration more informed, accessible, and purposeful, connecting scientific curiosity with the practical challenges of exploring another planet.
